items.type: Leadership committee of Gov. Brian Kemp
items.t: Gov. Brian Kemp's leadership committee. He set it up in 2021, as soon as a new state law took effect that lets a few top officials and party nominees run leadership committees that can raise unlimited money, even during a legislative session. In 2022, ruling on a lawsuit by his Republican primary challenger David Perdue, U.S. District Judge Mark Cohen barred it from spending to support Kemp's re-election or oppose his opponent during the primary and any primary runoff.
items.went: By May 9, 2022, it had raised $4.7 million since it was formed and spent all but $673,000, the AJC reported from its filings; the report does not break down what the money paid for.

items.type: Leadership committee of Lt. Gov. Burt Jones
items.t: Lt. Gov. Burt Jones's leadership committee. A 2021 state law created these committees for the governor, the lieutenant governor, the parties' nominees for those offices and legislative leaders; they can raise unlimited money, while other statewide candidates are held to $8,400 per donor for a primary and the general election and $4,800 for a runoff. It had $15.9 million on hand as of Jan. 31, 2026. On Feb. 20, 2026, ruling on a suit by Republican rival Rick Jackson, U.S. District Judge Thomas Thrash temporarily barred it from raising or spending money for Jones's campaign for governor and ordered the campaign ads it had bought since Feb. 10 canceled.
